name: pselect6
synopsis: int pselect(int nfds, fd_set *_Nullable restrict readfds, fd_set *_Nullable restrict writefds, fd_set *_Nullable restrict exceptfds, const struct timespec *_Nullable restrict timeout, const sigset_t *_Nullable restrict sigmask);
description: pselect() allows a program to monitor multiple file descriptors for I/O readiness while atomically modifying the signal mask to prevent race conditions. It is similar to select() but uses a timespec structure for timeout and includes a sigmask parameter for signal handling.

parameters.name: nfds
parameters.description: The highest-numbered file descriptor in any of the sets, plus 1.

parameters.name: readfds
parameters.description: Set of file descriptors to monitor for readability.

parameters.name: writefds
parameters.description: Set of file descriptors to monitor for writability.

parameters.name: exceptfds
parameters.description: Set of file descriptors to monitor for exceptions.

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: Timeout period for the wait, or NULL for no timeout.

parameters.name: sigmask
parameters.description: Signal mask to be atomically installed during the call.

return_value.success: Returns the number of file descriptors contained in the three returned descriptor sets.
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error

errors.description: An invalid file descriptor was given in one of the sets.
nfds is negative or exceeds the RLIMIT_NOFILE resource limit, or the value in timeout is invalid.
Unable to allocate memory for internal tables.

bugs: The glibc implementation has a fixed FD_SETSIZE limit of 1024, making it unsuitable for monitoring higher file descriptors; use poll(2) or epoll(7) instead. It is vulnerable to race conditions in older versions, and may report spurious readiness on sockets. Additionally, select() modifies timeout on interruption, which applies similarly to pselect().
